title: Gaussian binomial: scope and Mathlib gap
content: Building on the parent's quantum integer [n]_q, this file defines the Gaussian (q-)binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q directly by the q-Pascal recurrence and proves its structural laws. Mathlib has Nat.choose and the geometric sum but no named Gaussian binomial, no q-Pascal recurrence, and no q-binomial theorem. All results are 0-axiom.
mathContext: The Gaussian binomial $\binom{n}{k}_q$ is a polynomial in $q$ with $\binom{n}{k}_1 = \binom{n}{k}$. It counts $k$-dimensional subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, equals the box-partition generating function $\sum_{\lambda \subseteq (n-k)^k} q^{|\lambda|}$, and drives the Gauss/Rothe q-binomial theorem.

title: qBinom by the q-Pascal recurrence
content: qBinom q n k is defined by a two-argument structural recursion: [n choose 0]_q = 1, [0 choose k+1]_q = 0, and [n+1 choose k+1]_q = [n choose k]_q + q^{k+1}·[n choose k+1]_q. Defining by the recurrence makes q-Pascal and both boundary base cases hold by rfl.
mathContext: The q-Pascal rule $\binom{n}{k}_q = \binom{n-1}{k-1}_q + q^{k}\binom{n-1}{k}_q$ refines classical Pascal by the cocycle factor $q^{k}$; at $q=1$ it collapses to $\binom{n}{k} = \binom{n-1}{k-1} + \binom{n-1}{k}$. Defining $\binom{n}{k}_q$ this way avoids division in $\mathbb{Z}[q]$ that the quotient formula would require.

title: Boundary laws by structural recursion on the pair
content: qBinom_eq_zero_of_lt proves [n choose k]_q = 0 for n < k by recursion: the q-Pascal step reduces [n+1 choose k+1]_q to [n choose k]_q and [n choose k+1]_q, both zero since n < k. qBinom_self ([n choose n]_q = 1) then follows by induction, the off-diagonal term vanishing by qBinom_eq_zero_of_lt.
mathContext: These pin down the support of the q-Pascal triangle: $\binom{n}{k}_q \ne 0$ exactly on $0 \le k \le n$, with $1$'s along both boundaries $k=0$ and $k=n$.

title: The k=1 column is the quantum integer
content: qBinom_one_right: [n choose 1]_q = [n]_q. Proved by induction using the prepend recurrence [n+1]_q = q·[n]_q + 1 (qNat_succ', established from Finset.sum_range_succ'), which matches the q-Pascal step at k=0.
mathContext: The first column of the q-Pascal triangle reproduces the parent's quantum integer $[n]_q = 1 + q + \cdots + q^{n-1}$, so this entry sits directly on top of geometric-series-oq-04.

title: Classical limit: the counting interpretation
content: qBinom_at_one: [n choose k]_1 = C(n,k). Structural recursion whose successor step is exactly the classical Pascal identity Nat.choose_succ_succ (with q=1 collapsing q^{k+1} to 1), cast into R. The example [4 choose 2]_q = 1 + q + 2q^2 + q^3 + q^4 exhibits the polynomial whose q=1 value is C(4,2) = 6.
mathContext: At $q = 1$ the Gaussian binomial degenerates to the ordinary binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$, which counts the $k$-element subsets of an $n$-set. This is the $q=1$ shadow of the subspace count $\#\{W \le \mathbb{F}_q^n : \dim W = k\}$.
